Ovarian Chocolate Cyst (Endometrioma)

An ovarian chocolate cyst is a type of cyst formed due to endometriosis, where tissue similar to the inner lining of the uterus grows inside the ovary.
It contains old, dark blood—hence the name “chocolate cyst.”

Common Symptoms :

• Pelvic pain, especially during periods
• Pain during intercourse
• Heavy or irregular periods
• Difficulty conceiving 
• Sometimes, no symptoms at all

Why It Matters?

If untreated, these cysts can grow, cause pain, and may affect fertility. Early diagnosis helps in better management.

Treatment Options:

• Medicines to control symptoms
• Minimally invasive (laparoscopic) surgery for cyst removal
• Fertility-focused treatment when required

 If you experience persistent pelvic pain or menstrual discomfort, consult a specialist early.

**Dr Sharda Arvind**
Gynaecologist & Minimal Invasive Surgeon

🌸 Endometriosis & Fertility: What Patients Should Know

Struggling to conceive? Endometriosis could be one reason—but understanding it is the first step.

🔴 What is Endometriosis?
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, causing pain, inflammation, and scarring.

⚠️ How it affects fertility:

🚧 Blocked Fallopian Tubes
Scar tissue can prevent egg & sperm from meeting.

🥚 Ovarian Damage
Cysts (endometriomas) may affect egg quality and release.

🔥 Inflammation
Creates a hostile environment for fertilization and embryo development.

🏠 Implantation Issues
The uterus may be less receptive to pregnancy.

💡 The Good News
Many women with endometriosis DO conceive—naturally or with the right treatment.

👩‍⚕️ When to seek help?
• Trying >1 year (<35 years)
• Trying >6 months (>35 years)
• Painful periods or known endometriosis

📍 Early diagnosis = better fertility outcomes

📞 Book a consultation to explore your options

Symptoms of Endometriosis

Endometriosis can present in different ways—and symptoms may vary from person to person.

Common symptoms include:
• Severe pain during periods
• Pain during or after intercourse
• Chronic pelvic pain
• Heavy or irregular periods
• Pain while passing urine or stools (especially during periods)
• Bloating or digestive issues
• Difficulty in getting pregnant

These symptoms are often mistaken as “normal,” but they shouldn’t be ignored.

Early diagnosis can help manage pain and protect your fertility.

💬 If you have persistent symptoms, consult a specialist.

Endometriosis doesn’t affect just the uterus—it can involve multiple organs in the body.

Commonly affected areas include the ovaries, fallopian tubes, bowel, bladder, and pelvic lining. In rare cases, it can even involve the lungs and diaphragm.

This is why symptoms can vary—from severe period pain to bowel, bladder, or even chest-related discomfort.

Early diagnosis and the right treatment can help prevent complications and improve quality of life.

💬 If you have persistent pain or unusual symptoms, don’t ignore them—seek expert care.

Endometriosis is real—and so is the delay in diagnosis.
Many women suffer for years before getting the right answer.

If you have severe period pain, pain during intercourse, or ongoing pelvic discomfort, don’t ignore it. These symptoms are not “normal.”

Early diagnosis can help reduce pain, protect fertility, and improve quality of life.

If you’re experiencing symptoms, seek help. You don’t have to suffer in silence.

Endometriosis can have many causes—and often, it’s not just one reason.
It may be linked to hormone changes, genetics, immune system issues, or even the way menstrual flow happens.

If you have severe period pain, don’t ignore it—your body is trying to tell you something. Early diagnosis can make a big difference.

Did you know that millions of women worldwide live with endometriosis, often in silence? This condition can cause chronic pain, heavy periods, fatigue, and even fertility challenges—yet it is still widely misunderstood and underdiagnosed.

We believe awareness is the first step toward better care. If you or someone you know is experiencing symptoms, don’t ignore them. Early diagnosis and the right support can make a significant difference in quality of life.

I wanted her to hear the smile in my voice.

There was a pause. Then tears. Then laughter. Then both together.

"That is the reason behind our smiles."

Not statistics.
Not reports.

and a long wait finally whispers, “It was worth it.” 

From Dreams to Cradle!

Some journeys to parenthood are quiet.

Each time, they walked out holding reports… and unspoken tears.

There was no clear reason.
No obvious diagnosis.

Before recommending any treatment, I take a step back.

My first priority is not a report, a scan, or a standard protocol.
It is understanding you and the complete clinical context.

I start by listening carefully to your symptoms—how long they’ve been present, how they affect your daily life, and whether they have changed over time. Pain, bleeding patterns, bloating, or fatigue often tell a story that reports alone cannot.

Next, I review your medical and surgical history in detail. Previous treatments, medications, surgeries, and outcomes all influence what the right next step should be. What worked before matters just as much as what didn’t.

Your age, life stage, and future plans are equally important. Treatment decisions look very different for someone planning pregnancy, someone managing chronic pain, or someone approaching menopause.

I also evaluate whether intervention is truly needed at that point. Not every condition requires immediate treatment, and not every problem needs surgery. Sometimes observation, lifestyle changes, or medical management is the safer and more effective choice.

When surgery is considered, the focus is always on precision, minimal invasion, and long-term benefit, not speed or volume.

Every woman responds differently. That’s why I don’t follow templates.
I follow evidence, experience, and what is right for that individual patient.
